Both concern smaller Stroop interference while standing. Retain both printed partial eta-squared candidates without selecting a test or converting to ordinary eta-squared. Original-data candidate: partial eta-squared .155, F(1, 49) = 8.964, p = .004 (exact). Rescaled-data candidate: partial eta-squared .120, F(1, 49) = 6.693, p = .013 (exact). The latter scales each observer’s data to the overall mean across sitting and standing. The .130 value concerns the overall response-time posture main effect rather than Stroop interference; the sitting/standing Cohen’s d values concern within-posture Stroop effects, so they do not resolve the assigned comparison.
